title: SIM swap fraud - liability of banks and telecom companies
p1:
Your phone suddenly stops showing network. Minutes later, money starts disappearing from your bank account. Could someone really take control of your number without touching your phone?

SIM swap fraud works by criminals getting a duplicate SIM issued using your identity details and then receiving your calls and OTPs.
p2:
Many people think banks are always responsible for such losses. The reality is more complex. Liability may depend on whether the bank, telecom company, or customer failed to follow required security measures.

A surprising fact: once a SIM is swapped, criminals may not need your banking password if they can intercept verification messages.
p3:
Banks are expected to use proper security systems, while telecom companies must follow procedures before issuing replacement SIMs. Customers also play a role by reporting unusual network loss quickly and avoiding sharing personal information.

The key takeaway: losing mobile connectivity unexpectedly can be a financial warning sign, not just a technical issue.
conclusion: Do you think banks and telecom companies should automatically compensate victims of SIM swap fraud, or should responsibility be shared based on who failed to prevent the misuse?
